evidence.claim: Abdur Rouf Talukder joined as the 12th governor of Bangladesh Bank on 12 July 2022 after a long finance-ministry career; the bio says he contributed to budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.title: Mr. Abdur Rouf Talukder Former Governor, Bangladesh Bank
evidence.excerpt: Abdur Rouf Talukder joined as the 12th governor of Bangladesh Bank on 12 July 2022 after a long finance-ministry career; the bio says he contributed to budget reform, macroeconomic management, and IT in public financial management.
evidence.source_locator: bio paragraphs identifying his appointment and prior roles
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official biography page from the central bank, with direct appointment and career details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The page does not show Sheikh Hasina ordering the appointment, but it documents the government-selected central-bank leadership available to her administration.
contrary_evidence: The same bio shows a senior finance-ministry insider, so it supports competence but also suggests closeness to the executive rather than institutional independence.

evidence.claim: The e-GP portal brought public procurement online, cut procurement costs by about 7 percent, reduced tender time from 100 days to 57 days, processed 80 percent of public procurement expenditure in FY21, and improved integrity by reducing external influences and preserving audit trails.
evidence.title: World Bank-Funded Project Drives Public Procurement Reform in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The e-GP portal brought public procurement online, cut procurement costs by about 7 percent, reduced tender time from 100 days to 57 days, processed 80 percent of public procurement expenditure in FY21, and improved integrity by reducing external influences and preserving audit trails.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank results page with concrete implementation and outcome metrics.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective but highly relevant to 2022 governance conditions
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level reform implementation under the Hasina administration; the result page does not prove personal oversight by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The need to strengthen procurement integrity implies prior corruption and influence risks were material.

evidence.claim: The FY2022-23 budget speech made inflation control, a competitive exchange rate, continued economic development, employment generation, and emergency support for low-income people explicit priorities, including a Tk 5,000 crore fund for shocks from natural disasters or other crises.
evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The FY2022-23 budget speech made inflation control, a competitive exchange rate, continued economic development, employment generation, and emergency support for low-income people explicit priorities, including a Tk 5,000 crore fund for shocks from natural disasters or other crises.
evidence.source_locator: Chapter Seven and the low-income support section, lines 894-901 and 1237-1242
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government budget speech with explicit policy priorities and allocations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect. The document is the finance minister's budget speech for the Hasina government; it reflects administration priorities, not a direct personal statement by Hasina.
contrary_evidence: The speech is aspirational and does not itself prove successful execution.

evidence.claim: The budget allocated Tk 183,425 crore to social infrastructure, Tk 31,761 crore to primary and mass education, Tk 29,282 crore to health, Tk 44,690 crore to local government and rural development, and Tk 4,290 crore to women and children affairs; it also said social safety-net coverage had reached 29 percent of households and allocations had risen almost eight-fold since FY2008-09.
evidence.title: National Budget Speech 2022-2023
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The budget allocated Tk 183,425 crore to social infrastructure, Tk 31,761 crore to primary and mass education, Tk 29,282 crore to health, Tk 44,690 crore to local government and rural development, and Tk 4,290 crore to women and children affairs; it also said social safety-net coverage had reached 29 percent of households and allocations had risen almost eight-fold since FY2008-09.
evidence.source_locator: Chapter Six and social-safety-net section, lines 1028-1033, 1799-1801, 5651-5654, 2403-2406, and 2515-2519
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget text with explicit sectoral allocations and social-protection targets.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect government policy under the Hasina administration; the speech itself is by the finance minister, not Hasina personally.
contrary_evidence: The speech reports planned rather than audited outcomes, so implementation remains to be verified.

evidence.claim: Hasina announced that her government would build Smart Bangladesh by 2041 and said the strategy rests on smart citizens, smart economy, smart government, and smart society.
evidence.title: From 'Digital Bangladesh' to 'Smart Bangladesh' by 2041: PM
evidence.excerpt: Hasina announced that her government would build Smart Bangladesh by 2041 and said the strategy rests on smart citizens, smart economy, smart government, and smart society.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct public announcement by the ruler with clear date and context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: Hasina announced the goal herself as head of government.
contrary_evidence: Announcement is not the same as economy-wide implementation.

evidence.claim: The Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 frames a 100-year vision for a safe, climate-resilient and prosperous delta and a mission to ensure long-term water and food security, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.
evidence.title: Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100: Issues and Challenges of Implementation, 2022 conference page
evidence.excerpt: The Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 frames a 100-year vision for a safe, climate-resilient and prosperous delta and a mission to ensure long-term water and food security, economic growth, and environmental sustainability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official planning portal summarizing the national strategy in plain language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the plan is state strategy under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: The page sets goals and mission, not outcomes.

evidence.claim: A Delta Governing Council chaired by the prime minister had been set up to implement the Delta Plan 2100 through policy making, strategic direction, investment planning, and Delta Fund setup.
evidence.title: Delta Governing Council (DGC)
evidence.excerpt: A Delta Governing Council chaired by the prime minister had been set up to implement the Delta Plan 2100 through policy making, strategic direction, investment planning, and Delta Fund setup.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government implementation page describing the governing body and its duties.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: this is PM-chaired institutional machinery created under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: Institutional setup does not by itself prove effective execution.

evidence.claim: The Power Division won the Digital Bangladesh Award 2022 for ERP implementation that improved efficiency, transparency, accountability, and customer service, and the article says the system had been implemented across 15 subordinate bodies.
evidence.title: Power Division receives 'Digital Bangladesh Award 2022'
evidence.excerpt: The Power Division won the Digital Bangladesh Award 2022 for ERP implementation that improved efficiency, transparency, accountability, and customer service, and the article says the system had been implemented across 15 subordinate bodies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting with concrete implementation details and a named award.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government operational line under Hasina; the article credits agency-level execution more than personal micromanagement.
contrary_evidence: The benefits are reported by the division and the article, not independently audited in this item.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh's 20-month COVID-19 school closures led the Ministry of Education to create a remote learning strategy using television, radio, digital lessons, and printed materials that supported 150,933 children from marginalized groups in 842 schools.
evidence.title: Learning from the education sector’s COVID-19 response to prepare for future emergencies (Bangladesh)
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh's 20-month COVID-19 school closures led the Ministry of Education to create a remote learning strategy using television, radio, digital lessons, and printed materials that supported 150,933 children from marginalized groups in 842 schools.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF summary of a ministry-led response with explicit coverage figures and delivery channels.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Ministry of Education action under the Hasina government; this is not direct personal micromanagement.
contrary_evidence: The measure was a partial response to severe school disruption, not full continuity of schooling.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Bangladesh had achieved impressive growth and social development but still needed productive investment in infrastructure, human capital, and climate resilience to reach upper-middle-income status in 2031.
evidence.title: Bangladesh: 2021 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Bangladesh had achieved impressive growth and social development but still needed productive investment in infrastructure, human capital, and climate resilience to reach upper-middle-income status in 2031.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF country report summary with explicit policy and target language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but clear: the report addresses the authorities' stated development path under Hasina's government.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes pandemic interruptions, slowing poverty reduction, and financial vulnerabilities.

evidence.claim: The IMF and Bangladesh authorities reached a staff-level agreement for a new program aimed at preserving macroeconomic stability, supporting inclusive and green growth, and protecting the vulnerable, after reserves fell and the current-account deficit widened.
evidence.title: IMF Staff Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with Bangladesh on the Extended Credit Facility/Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility
evidence.excerpt: The IMF and Bangladesh authorities reached a staff-level agreement for a new program aimed at preserving macroeconomic stability, supporting inclusive and green growth, and protecting the vulnerable, after reserves fell and the current-account deficit widened.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IMF press release with concrete program design and contemporaneous macro stress context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the agreement was with the Bangladesh authorities led by Hasina's cabinet and central bank team.
contrary_evidence: The article also records reserve loss, inflation, and import-pressure stress, which constrain claims of clean success.

evidence.claim: Bangladesh navigated the COVID-19 pandemic with prudent macroeconomic policies and real GDP growth rebounded to 7.1 percent in FY22, supported by pandemic containment, domestic and external demand, and government stimulus packages and policy support.
evidence.title: Sustaining Growth in Bangladesh with Strong Reforms
evidence.excerpt: Bangladesh navigated the COVID-19 pandemic with prudent macroeconomic policies and real GDP growth rebounded to 7.1 percent in FY22, supported by pandemic containment, domestic and external demand, and government stimulus packages and policy support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank feature with explicit FY22 growth data and policy attribution, though still a retrospective synthesis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the growth rebound is policy-associated but also partly reflects inherited recovery and external demand.
contrary_evidence: The same source stresses inflation, BoP deficits, reserve pressure, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.

evidence.claim: Extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5.0 percent in 2022 from 9.0 percent in 2016, with improved infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitary toilets, and education access, though inequality and macro pressures persisted.
evidence.title: Structural Reforms are Essential to Sustain Growth & Poverty Reduction in Bangladesh
evidence.excerpt: Extreme poverty in Bangladesh fell to 5.0 percent in 2022 from 9.0 percent in 2016, with improved infant mortality, stunting, electricity access, sanitary toilets, and education access, though inequality and macro pressures persisted.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank feature based on 2022 household survey data and linked development update, with a methodological note.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate and limited: the gains reflect long-run growth and policy support rather than one 2022 decision alone.
contrary_evidence: The report notes methodological changes in the 2022 survey and still flags inflation, reserve pressure, and financial-sector vulnerabilities.
